research.topic: Info products, courses, cohorts, newsletters and communities about Claude Code / Codex / Agent Skills / AI-native operator work (EN + 中文): price points, revenue/subscriber evidence, time-to-first-dollar, and what sells

findings.claim: Paid Skool communities for Claude Code are the single fastest-growing paid shape in EN: Claude Code Club ~7,275-8,500 members at $9/mo founding price (rising to $69/mo), running since Aug 2025 and beginner/no-code positioned; a dozen others sit at $9-$184/mo with 95-3,800 members each (Claude Club $97/mo, 466 members; AItomation Academy ~$69/mo, 1,300+; AI Automations by Jack $87-97/mo, ~3.8k; Maker School $184/mo, ~2.2k). Founder revenue claims in this segment are self-reported and inconsistent (reviewers explicitly say 'read as marketing').
findings.evidence_date: 2026-07 to 2026-09 (member counts verified Jul/Sep 2026 by the directory sites)
findings.why_it_matters: Concrete money, not stars: even the mid-tier ($29-97/mo x 400-1,000 members) implies $12k-$97k/mo run-rate for a single operator with a YouTube funnel. The pattern that works is 'workflows 7-14 days before they hit YouTube' + skills/prompt library + weekly live Q&A, which maps exactly onto a bilingual blog+YouTube pipeline the founders already run.

findings.claim: Premium 2-week cohorts for Claude Code sell at $499-$799: AI Hero 'Claude Code for Real Engineers' 2-week cohort (Mar 30 2026, 6 office hours, Discord, lifetime access; prices shown dynamically, reported ~$795 with launch discounts); ByteByteGo 'Build with Claude Code' 2-day cohort $499 (May 28-29 2026, ex-Meta instructor, commenters pushed back on price); Maven 'Claude for Non-Technical Operators: Advanced Certification' $799 USD, Sep 29-Oct 12 2026, 4.9/5 from 63 reviews, targeting marketers/operators/founders, curriculum = Cowork config, building & testing custom Skills, subagents, plugins, MCP, scheduled tasks.
findings.why_it_matters: The Maven one is the closest comp to an 'AI-native operator' cohort: non-technical operators paying $799 to learn to build and test Skills. 63 reviews at $799 implies at least ~$50k gross across a few runs for one instructor. A cohort needs no build; time-to-first-dollar is the pre-sale window (2-4 weeks from announce).

findings.claim: Finance-professional-specific Claude training already sells and fills: Blend2Balance 'Claude in Action' 4x60-min live cohort for finance professionals (close, reporting, analysis; requires paid Claude plan) listed at $499 sale / $799 original for Sept 2026, Sept 2 cohort marked FULL, claims '1,000+ finance professionals trained', with a case study of a controller automating monthly reconciliation via a skill built in class. A separate Eventbrite 'Practical Claude Workshop for Finance & Accounting Professionals' ran Aug 21 2026 for CPAs.
findings.why_it_matters: Direct evidence that finance-flavored, operator-style Claude content has paying demand at ~$500-800/seat in small live groups, and that 'build a skill for your own reconciliation/reporting task' is the deliverable buyers cite. The founders' regulated wealth-ops depth is a differentiator no current seller has (Blend2Balance is accounting/FP&A, not asset management).

findings.claim: Low-ticket self-serve products for non-technical operators price at $30-60 and claim hundreds of buyers: 'Claude Code for Business' ($29.99, 7 modules, 150+ prompts, custom skills module, claims '500+ business owners'); 'Claude Code for Designers' on Gumroad $59.99 (333 skill files, 9 packs); Udemy 'Complete Claude Code & Claude Cowork Masterclass [2026]' exists (page blocked). Anthropic itself runs a free 10-city small-business workshop tour (from May 14 2026) and free Skilljar certificates (17 courses), which caps what basic-tutorial content can charge.
findings.why_it_matters: '500+ buyers x $30' is ~$15k, i.e. a low-ticket product is a lead magnet, not a business. Generic 'how to use Claude Code' is being given away by the vendor; only role-specific or domain-specific packaging (designers, business owners, finance) retains a price.

findings.claim: Skill packs sell on Gumroad at $49-$167 but with no disclosed sales and visible price resistance: 'Master Marketing Claude Skills Bundle' 167 skills for $167; 'Claude Skills for Founders' (40 CLAUDE.md files); 'Claude Skills Pack' 30 files across writing/sales/legal/finance/HR; 'Premium Claude Skills Collection' (updated 2026-05-15); 'OpenClaw + Claude Code 24/7 Persistent Agent Playbook'. Round-1 digest found the only explicit price reaction to an '84-skill pack $49' was negative, and free packs (superpowers 284k stars, mattpocock/skills 258k stars, ~60k newsletter) dominate attention.
findings.why_it_matters: Stars, not money: skill packs are a distribution/lead asset. The founders' 32 skills should be a free funnel into a paid community/cohort/service, not the product. Attention in this ecosystem accrues to free packs; the paid layer is instruction + access to the author.

findings.claim: Matt Pocock / AI Hero is the reference EN model: full-time AI-coding educator, free email course -> self-paced 'AI Coding Crash Course' -> 2-week 'Claude Code / AI Coding for Real Engineers' cohort ($795 class), a free MIT skills repo (258k stars) as top-of-funnel, ~60k newsletter subscribers (round-1 digest) and 100k+ X followers. Workshops page not fetchable (404).
findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the ladder shape (free skills repo -> newsletter -> $795 cohort). Note the presence of pirated-course resale sites (udcourse.com) for his cohort: a sign of real demand and a reason to sell access/live time, not just recordings.

findings.claim: Tessl Academy (preview launched 2026-07-07; 'Skill Foundations', a second course, and 'Code Review Loops' added 2026-08-21) is free, hands-on curriculum for building/evaluating/running skills; Tessl's platform is free-tier and monetizes teams/enterprise, not learners. Anthropic Academy on Skilljar (launched 2026-03-02, 17 free courses incl. Claude Code and Agent Skills, free certificates) is also free.
findings.why_it_matters: Vendor and incumbent education on 'how skills work' is free. Paid info products must sell something the vendor cannot: a specific domain (finance ops), a specific persona (non-technical operator), the creator's live judgment, or a community.

findings.claim: Newsletter economics for 'how I run my business/newsletter on Claude Code' content: AI Maker Substack went 0 -> 9,700+ subscribers and $30k+ ARR in ~8 months (launched 2025-04-02, paid tier turned on ~4 months in), reporting that 'complete implementation blueprints' for AI workflows are what paid readers buy and that recommendation-sourced subscribers convert poorly (17% of subs, 5% of paid revenue). Median newsletter converts ~0.62% to paid at ~$10/mo. beehiiv paid subs grew 138% to $19M in 2025.
findings.why_it_matters: A paid newsletter is slow money (4 months to first paid dollar, $30k ARR at ~10k subs). It works as the retention layer for a community/cohort, not as the first bet. 'Implementation blueprints' is the content unit that converts, which matches the founders' operator style.

findings.claim: 中文市场：付费社群/课程价格锚点明确。OpenClaw(Claude Code 衍生 agent 框架) 变现文章给出教育类定价 99元基础课 / 299元进阶 / 999元一对一，模板 9.9-99元，社群 199-999元/月，'代部署' 100元/次、项目 500-3000元、'已卖700+单 7万+收入'；网易号列出多家 OpenClaw 知识星球（AI小宇宙等）互相竞争。这些是营销口径的自述收入，非审计数字。
findings.why_it_matters: Chinese price ceiling for agent-tool education is roughly 1/5-1/8 of EN ($15-140 per course vs $500-800), but volume and 'done-for-you deployment' (100-3,000元 per job) are the real money shapes. Expect a bilingual play to earn on the EN side and use 中文 for reach.

findings.claim: 中文平台数据：极客时间《Claude Code 工程化实战》(黄佳, 23讲音频 + 10章纸书 + 直播加餐) 定价 ¥69 (返现平台 ¥51)，新人首单 ¥59；讲师同步开 '多 Agent 设计与工程化' 训练营（早鸟后涨价）。小报童 AI 榜：'AI海外赚钱' 16,317 订阅 @ ¥10，'AI入门到变现' 10,300 @ ¥19.9，'编程与AI编程' 4,056 @ ¥18.8，'小七姐的AI提示词' 4,491 @ ¥99；而专门的 'Claude变现指南：100个赚钱方案' 仅 25 订阅 @ ¥99 早鸟 (定价 ¥599)。B站充斥免费 'Claude Code 保姆级教程'，标题常带 '吊打付费'。
findings.why_it_matters: In 中文, what sells at scale is '用AI赚钱/海外赚钱' framing at ¥10-30 (mass), not tool tutorials (¥69, or 25 subs at ¥99). 'AI海外赚钱' at 16k subs is the strongest demand signal for a bilingual, overseas-based operator voice. Tool-specific Chinese content is commoditized by free B站 tutorials.

findings.claim: 中文金融+社群需求存在但监管在收紧：知识星球畅销榜长期由股票/基金内容主导（搜索摘要引述某财经博主 1.7万成员 x 1,499元/年，未能直接核实）；2026-01-29 知识星球启动金融专项整治（清查'非法经济学家'、无资质课程、非法荐股），今日头条同步要求付费圈子圈主具备证券从业资格。Anthropic 2026-05-05 开源 Claude for Financial Services (10 agents/41->56 skills/11 connectors) 在掘金、53AI、腾讯云、21经济 等中文媒体获得密集解读。
findings.why_it_matters: Demand for finance-flavored AI content in 中文 is high (Chinese media eagerly translate Anthropic's finance skills), but 'investment advice' framing is now policed on 知识星球/头条. The safe, differentiated lane is 'wealth-management OPERATIONS workflows on Claude' (look-through reports, proposals, dashboards) — operator craft, not stock picks.

findings.claim: Non-technical operators (Cowork users) are an explicitly targeted, paying segment: Claude Cowork (launched 2026-01-12, Pro+ plans) is covered as 'Claude Code for non-programmers' in 中文/日文 media; EN offerings for this persona include the $799 Maven certification, Skool communities at $9-97/mo, and a 3-evening 'Claude Code Workshop for Beginners' (May 29-Jun 1 2026, marketers/solopreneurs/employees).
findings.why_it_matters: Round-1 found individual developers do not pay for skill tooling; this angle shows non-developers DO pay for instruction on skills/Cowork. The founders' day-job business users asking for skill workflows are this persona.

price_points_observed: Skool communities: $9/mo founding (Claude Code Club, ->$69), $29/mo (Agentic Labs), $69/mo (AItomation Academy), $83/mo or $497/yr (AI Captains), $87-97/mo (AI Automations by Jack, Claude Club), $97/mo (Vibe Coding Academy), $184/mo (Maker School)

Finance-professional live cohort: $499 sale / $799 list (Blend2Balance Claude in Action, 4x60min)
Self-serve low ticket: $29.99 (Claude Code for Business), $59.99 (Claude Code for Designers)
Gumroad skill packs: $49 (84-skill pack), $167 (167 marketing skills)
Paid newsletter: ~$10/mo median; $30k ARR at ~9.7k subs example
中文 极客时间专栏: ¥69 list / ¥51-59 promo (Claude Code 工程化实战)
中文 小报童: ¥10-¥30 mass columns (10k-16k subs), ¥99 prompt column (4.5k subs), ¥99 early-bird/¥599 list Claude 变现 column (25 subs)
中文 OpenClaw education: 99/299/999元 course tiers, 9.9-99元 templates, 199-999元/月 社群, 100元 代部署, 500-3,000元 per project
Free floor: Anthropic Academy (17 courses + certificates), Tessl Academy, Anthropic small-business workshop tour, B站 保姆级教程
fastest_money_shapes: Paid live cohort/workshop for a named persona (finance/ops professionals or non-technical operators), $499-$799/seat, 4 sessions over 2-4 weeks, capped at 15-30 seats, sold via the existing blog/YouTube/X audience. Time-to-first-dollar: 1-3 weeks (pre-sale on announcement; Blend2Balance filled a Sept cohort; Maven/AI Hero sell weeks ahead). 30-day pass/fail: 10 paid seats.

Paid community (Skool/Discord/微信群) at $29-97/mo (EN) or 199-999元/月 (中文) fed by 'workflows 7-14 days before YouTube' + the 32-skill library as members-only installs + weekly live Q&A. Time-to-first-dollar: days (founding-member price), but needs ~100 members to matter. 30-day pass/fail: 50 paying members.

Done-for-you skill build / 'skills sprint' productized service for a small firm or team ($2-10k EN; 500-3,000元 per project 中文 comp), sold to the business users already asking for Claude-skill workflows and to cohort alumni. Time-to-first-dollar: 2-4 weeks (one deal). Highest $/hour, doubles as customer discovery.

Low-ticket self-serve playbook/skill-pack ($29-59 EN; ¥19-99 中文) as lead magnet with a paid upgrade path. Time-to-first-dollar: 1-2 weeks after publishing, but ceiling is ~$10-15k unless it feeds a cohort/community.
Paid newsletter/专栏 (Substack $10/mo; 小报童 ¥10-99) — slowest: ~4 months to first paid dollar at the reference case, $30k ARR at ~10k subs. Use as retention layer, not as a 30-day bet.
open_questions: No seller in EN or 中文 discloses audited revenue; all community/course revenue is inferred from members x price or self-reported. Which of the $9/mo Skool member counts are active payers vs churned?

Does the finance-professional cohort demand (Blend2Balance 1,000+ trained, accounting/FP&A) extend to asset/wealth-management operations staff specifically, and would they buy from a Canada-based bilingual seller? No direct comp found.

知识星球 finance-community numbers (17k members @ ¥1,499/yr) came from a search summary and could not be verified at source; actual 知识星球 pricing for AI-tool communities was not directly observable (login-walled).

Chinese demand for BILINGUAL operator content specifically is inferred from '海外赚钱' column popularity (16k subs @ ¥10), not from any direct comp of an overseas Chinese creator monetizing Claude Code content; no such creator with disclosed numbers was found.
How much does Anthropic's free tour/Academy and Tessl Academy compress the price of generic Claude Code instruction over the next 2 quarters? Only persona/domain-specific offers appear insulated.
Time-to-first-dollar figures for cohorts/communities are inferred from launch-to-cohort gaps on public pages, not from operators' own disclosures.

research.topic: Productized Claude/Codex skill, Cowork plugin and agent-workflow services for SMBs and professional-services firms: pricing, freelance rates, who sells it, how clients are found, time-to-first-dollar, and what SMB buyers say they need (evidence as of 2026-09-10)

findings.claim: A working, explicitly priced 'we set up Claude Cowork for your firm' package already exists at small-agency scale: Wellforce (an MSP) sells a one-time flat fee of $2,500-$9,500 (legal deployments from $3,500) covering plan selection, setup, 2-3 connected tools, a starter prompt + Skills library the client keeps, two training sessions and a one-page AI use policy, 'live in about two weeks'. Target verticals listed: nonprofits, law firms, associations, dealerships, healthcare, government contractors, financial services. No customer count disclosed.
findings.why_it_matters: Direct comparable for the fastest money shape: a fixed-fee 2-week Cowork/Skills install for a 2-50 person professional-services firm, priced in the C$3-12k band, no procurement, delivered by a tiny team. Money, not stars.

findings.claim: A second solo/boutique shop, 8th Street Solutions, prices the same offer at $2,000-$5,000 fixed setup (three weeks: plan/orientation, work skills & tools, training/launch) plus $500-$1,500/month retainers; explicit ICP is 'small to mid-sized businesses, two to fifty people' incl. law firms, accounting practices, financial advisory, consultancies and contractors 'past the experimenting stage'. Content updated Aug 2026; no customer count.
findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the price floor and the 3-week delivery shape for skills-authoring + connectors + training; the $500-1,500/mo retainer is the recurring layer a 2-person team can carry at 5-10 clients.

findings.claim: Claude Code-specific consulting rates cluster at $100-$300/hr for senior independents; engagement menu is a 3-5 day audit, a 1-3 week 'setup sprint' (CLAUDE.md, hooks, MCP, security rules), embedded engineer 1-6 months, or monthly retainer; one agency (AY Automate) publishes $4,500+ discovery and $12k-$50k builds; broader agency bands are $5k for a 'small scoped Claude Code build' up to $250k+.
findings.why_it_matters: Sets the hourly and fixed-price anchors for the engineer-side offer (Claude Code setup sprint for a dev team) that Founder B could deliver in evenings; $4.5k audit -> $12k+ build is a proven ladder.

findings.claim: Anthropic's own SMB motion lowers the buyer's cost to near zero but leaves a services gap: 'Claude for Small Business' (launched 2026-05-13) is a free Cowork plugin with 15 workflows + 15 skills and QuickBooks/PayPal/HubSpot/Canva/DocuSign/Google/M365 connectors; an independent review (2026-05-18) prices total SMB cost at $1,500-$5,940/yr and names the residual gaps as operational training (4-6 weeks supervised review), connector setup/auth across seven tools, and 'how to recover when a workflow misfires' / auditing AI-touched accounting entries.
findings.why_it_matters: The vendor gives the skills away; what SMBs still pay for is configuration, firm-specific skills, training and 'did it fire / what did it produce' recovery — exactly the evidence/fixture discipline in the founders' POC, repackaged as a service.

findings.claim: Non-developer skill authors' pain is documented and unresolved: a 2026 audit found 73% of 214 community Claude skills scored below 60/100 and 'most failed silently'; user complaints quoted include 'Claude still loves to ignore skills' and a business user whose skills 'are all loading at once'. Cowork Team plans soft-cap 50 custom skills; practitioners say most businesses run 8-15 before the list becomes 'a junk drawer' and recommend a skill only when a task recurs 4+ times/month.
findings.why_it_matters: A 'skills audit + fix' fixed-fee offer (inventory, dedupe, trigger descriptions, fixtures, junk-drawer cleanup) maps directly to observed pain and to the founders' existing tooling; it is a cheap, fast first product for firms already on Cowork.

findings.claim: Per-workflow and retainer benchmarks for SMB AI automation (2026): single workflow builds $2,500-$12,000 (some guides $5-15k), pilots $5-15k, SMB retainers $500-$2,000/month (Digital Agency Network), $1,000-$3,500/month for 2-3 monitored workflows, mid-market retainers $3-8k/month, SMB AI audits $2-8k; DAN's own guide lists AI automation setup $2,500-$15,000+ and monitoring retainers $500-$5,000+, AI consulting $100-$450/hr.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'one workflow, fixed price' unit is already a market norm at $2.5-12k; the founders can price a Claude-skill workflow inside this band without educating buyers on 'skills'.

findings.claim: Upwork demand data: top AI-application skills grew 109% YoY, 'AI integration' work (connecting AI into existing business systems) grew 178% YoY; freelancers doing AI work earn 34% more per hour; complex AI-augmented work earnings +45% while per-contract pay for simple generative tasks fell 13%. Practitioner rate bands for AI-automation freelancers: entry $25-40/hr, mid $50-85/hr, experienced production builds $100-180+/hr; senior AI/ML $100-300/hr. But the AI&ML category is 'over-fished' (proposal reply rate 7.21% vs 7.45% platform mean; 3,535 AI proposals in a 133,872 sample) and Upwork active clients fell 6% YoY to 784k.
findings.why_it_matters: Demand for integration/agent work is real and premium-priced, but marketplaces are crowded and low-reply; Upwork is a rate benchmark and a fallback channel, not the founders' fastest route to a first client.

findings.claim: Upwork has live 'Claude'-specific postings and specialists: a dedicated 'Claude specialists' hire page (Sep 2026), jobs titled 'Set up Claude Code and VS Code', 'Claude Code Training' and 'Claude AI Agent Expert For Automation' (all <30 hrs/week, <1 month), and at least one specialist selling a $499 fixed 'automation audit' (5-10 business days); search summaries cite client budgets 'typically $5K+' targeting '$10K+ in measurable savings within 90 days'. Job pages returned 403 to fetch, so budgets are unverified.
findings.why_it_matters: Buyers are literally posting 'set up Claude Code for me' and 'train my team on Claude Code' as sub-one-month gigs; a $499 fixed audit is the smallest observed money shape and a plausible 30-day pass/fail lead magnet.

findings.claim: Training is a separately priced, fast-to-sell SKU: Claude training providers quote one-off workshops at $2,000-$7,500 per session (one vendor 'from $4,500'), executive 1:1 from $5,000, 90-day rollouts from $42,500, ongoing advisory $1,800-$5,000/month, freelance consultants $150-$300/hr; a rule of thumb pitched to buyers is '$2-3 in training per $1 of AI tools' (e.g., $14.4-21.6k training on 20 seats).
findings.why_it_matters: A half-day 'Claude/Cowork for your firm' workshop at $2-5k needs no build and can close in days; it doubles as discovery for the skills-build package. Founder A's bilingual content pipeline is the natural funnel.

findings.claim: Vertical implementers for accounting, law and advisory firms have appeared with published menus: Phos AI Labs ~$10,000/month 3-phase retainer for $5M+ accounting firms; LOW/CODE Agency sprint-based for $1-20M firms; Layer3 Labs (free 30-min audit, recommends 'ship one Skill per week for four weeks') publishes named skill lists for CPA firms (close narratives, reconciliation notes, PBC responses, 1040 review checklists, engagement letters, K-1 explainers, workpaper summaries), law firms (8 workflows) and advisors (8 workflows: meeting recaps, IPS, quarterly letters, TLH, fee explainer, KYC, prospect research, portfolio review prep) with a 3-week rollout and 'every Skill goes through CCO review'. Automaton (law) offers free 24-hour scorecards and 90-day deployment guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Shows the productized-skills menu buyers respond to (named workflows, one-skill-per-week cadence, CCO sign-off) and that competitors acquire via SEO guides + free audits; the founders' wealth-ops depth fits the advisor/asset-manager menu where fewer implementers publish.

findings.claim: Attention, not money: skill packs and courses sell cheaply. Gumroad 'Master Marketing Claude Skills Bundle' (167 skills) lists at $167; a marketplace guide reports individual SKILL.md listings at $5-15 (up to $25), 'top-earning individual skills roughly $500-$3,000/month', 'median listed skill earns less than $50/month', top 10% take most revenue, 30% platform fee; a monetization guide says the models 'generating real revenue right now' are the behind-the-scenes service (setup fee + monthly retainer) and internal/white-label licensing, while selling files 'leaks IP'. An advisor-niche newsletter (Amplify for Advisors) monetizes skills as a $20/month paid-subscriber perk.
findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the w1 conclusion for this angle: packs are distribution/lead-gen (hundreds of dollars/month at best), the service around the skill is where thousands per client are. Use packs as the content-pipeline funnel, not the business.

findings.claim: How boutiques get clients and how long it takes: a CRM consultancy's published playbook says '8-16 weeks from initial training to first billable AI engagement', fastest channel is the existing client base, then Partner Network co-sell, then content; it prices strategy assessments $15-50k and retainers $5-25k/month (mid-market, not SMB). Anthropic's Claude Partner Network (opened 2026-03-12, free to join; Services Track added 2026-06-03) had 40,000 firm applicants and 10,000+ certified consultants by June; entry 'Select' tier needs 10 certified practitioners, 2 production joint customers and 1 public story — out of reach for a 2-person shop, so referral from Anthropic is not a near-term channel.
findings.why_it_matters: Time-to-first-client of 2-4 months for firms starting cold; the founders' warm network (day-job business users, personal audience) is the only way to hit 30-60 days. Partner Network is crowded (40k applicants) and tier-gated — do not plan on it.

findings.claim: Cowork private plugin marketplaces (2026-02-24) let Team/Enterprise admins curate, auto-install and per-user provision plugins, build them from templates with Claude's guidance, and load partner-built plugins (Tribe AI's Brand Voice, LSEG, S&P, Apollo, Common Room, Slack); private GitHub-repo plugin publishing is in private beta; Anthropic publishes a financial-services-plugins repo as a starting template. No pricing or third-party monetization path for plugin sellers exists — plugins are delivered as part of services.
findings.why_it_matters: A 'firm-specific Cowork plugin' (skills + connectors + commands in the client's private marketplace) is the deliverable format; it is installable by the client's admin without IT projects, which keeps the sales cycle SMB-fast. There is no plugin store revenue — charge for the build.

findings.claim: Micro-evidence of very small first dollars: playbook posts report a freelancer charging local small businesses a flat $150 to organize spreadsheets and set up plain-English Claude Q&A, another claiming $4,200/month as a Claude Code + Gemini automation freelancer, and a '$2,840 in 30 days' Claude playbook (Medium, Jul 2026; article body not retrievable). Guides consistently say the fastest first client is an existing client/contact, not cold prospecting; generic 'AI agency' blueprints ($39/month Gumroad etc.) are content products, not businesses.
findings.why_it_matters: Self-reported and unverifiable, but they bracket the low end: first dollars in days at $150-$500 tickets via warm/local outreach; a solo operator plateau of ~$4k/month without productization.

findings.claim: Chinese-language market signal is attention-only: high-traffic 2026 articles on woshipm/53AI/Zhihu list '18 high-value Claude Skills by job role', '38 admin skills' with WeChat Work/DingTalk integrations, etc., but none carry pricing or consulting offers; no ZH-language 'we build Claude skills for your firm' offer with a price was found.
findings.why_it_matters: A bilingual content pipeline can win attention in ZH quickly, but the paid-services evidence is entirely EN/North America; treat ZH as audience-building, not a 30-60 day revenue bet, unless a specific ZH buyer is already in hand.

Training: workshops $2,000-$7,500/session (from $4,500), exec 1:1 from $5,000, 90-day rollout from $42,500, advisory $1,800-$5,000/mo

Platform cost the buyer already pays: Claude Team $20-25/seat/mo (Premium $100-125), Pro $17-20/mo; Claude for Small Business plugin free; SMB total $1,500-$5,940/yr
fastest_money_shapes: 1. Fixed-fee 'Claude/Cowork install + skills library' for a 2-50 person professional-services firm (law, CPA, advisory, consultancy): $2.5-9.5k, 2-3 weeks, deliverable = private Cowork plugin (8-15 firm-specific skills + 2-3 connectors) + 2 training sessions + one-page AI policy; optional $500-1,500/mo retainer. Time-to-first-dollar: 1-4 weeks if sold to a warm contact (day-job business users, personal audience), 8-16 weeks cold. 30-day test: 1 signed at >= C$3k.

2. Paid 'skills audit / did-it-fire' fix for firms already on Cowork or Claude Code: $499-$2,500 fixed, 5-10 business days — inventory skills, dedupe the junk drawer, rewrite trigger descriptions, add 3-5 fixtures per skill, produce a before/after report. Maps to documented pain (73% of community skills fail silently; 'all loading at once'). Time-to-first-dollar: days; smallest ticket, best lead magnet for shape 1.

3. Half-day or 2-session 'Claude for your firm' workshop, $2-5k per session, sold through the bilingual blog/YouTube pipeline and LinkedIn; zero build, converts ~1 in 3 into a shape-1 install per agency guides' audit-to-retainer conversion. Time-to-first-dollar: 1-3 weeks.

4. Single-workflow fixed build for an SMB or advisory desk (e.g., quarterly letter, meeting recap, proposal draft, reconciliation notes) at $2.5-12k with a 4-week 'one skill per week' cadence and a named human sign-off gate; retainer $1-3.5k/mo for monitoring 2-3 workflows. Time-to-first-dollar: 30-60 days (scope + deposit), 40% upfront norms.

5. Claude Code 'setup sprint' for a small dev team (CLAUDE.md, hooks, MCP, guardrails, eval fixtures): $4.5k discovery -> $12k+ build, or $100-300/hr; deliverable by Founder B in evenings. Time-to-first-dollar: 2-6 weeks via Upwork/Contra-style postings ('Set up Claude Code', 'Claude Code Training') or warm dev-team contacts; Upwork itself is over-fished (7.2% reply rate), so treat it as benchmark/fallback.

research.topic: Micro-SaaS and small paid tools around agent skills / Claude Code / Codex with visible paying users (EN + ZH markets), 2026 — money vs. stars

findings.claim: Agensi (Amsterdam, Antler-backed) is the largest paid skill marketplace by attention: 2,000 skills, 3,000 registered users, 50,000 monthly visitors, 200+ creators three months after an ~April 2026 launch; buyer plans Free / $9 Starter / $19 Pro (credits at $0.16-0.20), creators keep 70% via Stripe Connect. But its own creator guide (Apr 30, 2026) reports the median listing earns under $50/month, revenue concentrates in the top ~10% of listings, and the only named top sellers are $6-9 skills with 12-89 installs ($75-$436 lifetime). No GMV or revenue disclosed.
findings.why_it_matters: This is 'has attention, not customers': a funded marketplace with 50k visitors/month still produces sub-$50/month per listing. Listing skills on a third-party marketplace is not a 30-60-day first-customer path; it is a distribution experiment at best.

findings.claim: KissMySkills (Shopify store, 1,097 skill files, 45 free) sells .skill ZIPs at $14.99 each, role bundles at $99 (list $160), 'Everything Bundle' $447.99 (list $1,760), with a 30-day money-back guarantee and a claimed 4.9/5 from 6,400+ reviews. Target buyer is explicitly the non-technical professional who uploads to Claude desktop Customize > Skills. Review count is self-reported and unverifiable; no revenue disclosed. Claude Protocol sells the same shape at $3.99-$78/skill and $99 for a 501-skill catalog.
findings.why_it_matters: The non-engineer 'paste a specialist into Claude' buyer is the one segment paying list price for skill files ($15-$99 impulse tier). It is a content/e-commerce business (SEO + Shopify), not a tooling business — and it is the shape the founders' bilingual content pipeline could copy in weeks.

findings.claim: Solo-creator skill packs sold to an existing audience are the only skill-file product with a verified time-to-first-dollar: an SEO-agency owner with a 10k newsletter / 39k YouTube audience sold a 25-40 skill 'Claude Code Skills Stack' at $99 and made ~$3,000 in 30-45 days with no ads; a third-party fact-check calls it 'half-true' because ~$1,000 came from a consulting upsell and the sales rode a pre-existing list, with realistic no-audience outcomes of $0-300 in 90 days. Gumroad comparables: 'OpenClaw + Claude Code Playbook' $57 with 12-14 sales visible; '300+ Claude Skills' at ~$2-50; a Sep 2025 HN reaction to an '$49 84-skill pack' was 'AI slop'.
findings.why_it_matters: Money arrives in 30-45 days only when an audience already exists; the pack is the receipt for the audience, not the product. With a bilingual blog+YouTube pipeline already running, a $49-99 pack is the cheapest 30-day pass/fail the founders can run — pass/fail number should be sales, not downloads.

findings.claim: Cohort courses are the highest-ticket 'skills' money visible: Maven 'Claude Code in Practice' at $1,500 is SOLD OUT for the Sep 2-Oct 4, 2026 cohort with 54 five-star reviews; DAIR 'Claude Code for Everyone' (explicitly non-technical welcome) at $899 per seat; AI Hero 'Claude Code for Real Engineers' ~$795; Gumroad self-paced 'Claudecademy Essential' $49 including a skill-authoring module. Anthropic's own Skilljar courses are free.
findings.why_it_matters: Sold-out $900-1,500 cohorts are 'has customers'. A 2-day 'skills for operators' or bilingual cohort needs ~10 seats to clear $10k, requires no build, and converts directly from the content pipeline. Time-to-first-dollar = the length of a launch email sequence (2-4 weeks).

findings.claim: Team training and Cowork implementation are priced and being bought as fixed-fee services: MentorCruise team workshops $250 (2h) / $500 (half-day) / $900 (full day); claudetraining.com custom workshop $4,500, series from $12,500, 90-day rollout from $42,500; a Cowork implementation shop charges a flat $2,500-$9,500 (legal from $3,500) for setup + connectors + a starter Skills library + two training sessions + a one-page AI policy, 'live in about two weeks'. No customer counts disclosed by any of them.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'starter Skills library + training + AI policy' bundle at $2.5-9.5k flat is the closest priced comparable to what business users at the day job are already asking for. It needs zero product build, closes in one call, and each engagement yields fixtures/rubrics the POC can reuse.

findings.claim: Claude Code usage/cost trackers: the only paid ones are tiny. SessionWatcher (macOS menu bar) sells from $6.99 one-time with a 7-day trial; Usagebar launched on Product Hunt as pay-what-you-want (172 upvotes, #6 of the day, 0 reviews, maker plans to open-source). Everything else is free: ccusage (18.5k stars, maintainer has 26 GitHub sponsors at $4-256/mo), Claude-Usage-Tracker, ClaudeUsageBar, Claude Tracker, CCUM, the built-in /usage, /cost (rebuilt in v2.1.92) and statusline. Torii's 5-tool roundup lists only itself (enterprise SaaS) as a paid third party.
findings.why_it_matters: Individual devs pay at most a one-time $7 for cost dashboards, and Anthropic ships the feature natively every few releases. 18.5k stars converts to 26 sponsors. Do not build a usage/cost dashboard as a money bet.

findings.claim: 'Did my skill fire' / trigger-testing tooling exists only as free OSS or free downloads: UiPath's coder-eval (Apache-2.0, precision/recall on ~1,000 labeled prompts, Jul 30, 2026), a free 'skill-routing-eval' kit (2 skills, 12 prompts, 4 outcome labels), Anthropic's skill-creator trigger-rate measurement, plus a wave of SEO troubleshooting posts (devencyclopedia, qaskills.sh, agentscamp) that monetize via course affiliate links, not tools. No paid product with customers found.
findings.why_it_matters: The pain is real (search volume drives content sites) but the money shape is the content/course funnel, not the checker. A 'skill trigger audit' fits as a free lead magnet or a paid 1-hour review, not as SaaS.

findings.claim: Skill sync/versioning/governance for teams: SkillRepo is the only priced product (Team from $8/seat/month, no minimum, 14-day trial, 1,731 graded skills A-F, version pinning, drift tracking, recall) and shows no customers, logos or testimonials; r/ClaudeCode mentions in a year: 0. Anthropic's Skills API (GA Aug 20, 2026) now does upload + immutable skver_* version pinning natively, and Cursor Teams ($40/seat) bundles a team skill marketplace.
findings.why_it_matters: Version history / sync with paid tiers has a priced comparable with zero visible traction and is being absorbed vendor-side. Not a 30-60 day money shape.

findings.claim: Hosted skills (agents as a service) is where a small operator shows real paying users: Agent37 reports 'more than 1,000 people pay for hosting today, across roughly 1,000 live instances' at $3.44-$3.99/month minimum plus metered usage (~$45k ARR order of magnitude), was #1 Product of the Day on Product Hunt, and argues file-based skills fail because 'piracy is trivial' and usage is invisible. No GMV for skills sold through it.
findings.why_it_matters: Even the best-evidenced micro-SaaS in the niche is ~1,000 customers x ~$4/month after a Product Hunt #1. That is the realistic ceiling for a self-serve tool here in year one — fine as a portfolio bet, not as the main bet.

findings.claim: China: ByteDance's Coze (扣子) launched a Skills Store with paid skills on Jan 19, 2026 (2.0 release). Creators set monthly subscription prices from 1 to 298 RMB/month, collect via Alipay/Douyin Pay after merchant KYC, must supply three use cases, and pass a ~5-business-day review; the store had 365+ skills plus official industry skills (law, finance, e-commerce, education) by early 2026. Secondary Chinese posts claim a PPT-beautification skill grossed 120,000 RMB in 3 weeks and a courseware skill averages 30,000 RMB/month; an official-channel roundup only says creator incomes 'range from 10k to 1M RMB' across knowledge products, custom development, contest prizes and template revenue-share (platform takes 20% on templates). The specific earnings claims could not be traced to a primary source.
findings.why_it_matters: Coze is the only skill store with per-call/subscription billing built in and consumer payment rails — a bilingual founder can list a finance/ops skill there in days. The money evidence is louder than the EN market but almost entirely secondary/marketing; treat as a cheap test, not a validated channel.

findings.claim: China enterprise side: DingTalk 'WuKong' (悟空, announced Mar 17, 2026) ships an 'AI capability market' compatible with the open SKILL.md ecosystem with a dev-review-list-distribute pipeline and a stated goal of being 'the largest toB Skill market' (installed base 20M+ organizations); Feishu upgraded Aily and shipped a CLI agent on Mar 19, 2026. Alibaba Cloud's Agent Skills Portal explicitly states skills and plugins are free ('云 Agent 服务目录本身免费，Skills 与 Plugins 均可免费获取') with no developer monetization. No revenue-share terms were found for any of the three.
findings.why_it_matters: Chinese enterprise platforms are absorbing skill distribution as a free platform feature, same as Anthropic. The only Chinese money rail today is Coze's consumer/prosumer store; do not plan on DingTalk/Feishu/Alibaba marketplaces paying builders within 60 days.

findings.claim: Free directories dominate attention in both languages: skills.sh 1.42M skills, top skill 3.3M installs (all free); SkillsMP (Chinese-run, promoted on X by Chinese AI influencers) aggregates 26k-60k GitHub skills, free, no account; mcpmarket/skills.pub/AugmentClaude all free. Skill packs get 250k+ stars (superpowers, mattpocock) while priced tools get 0-50. Chinese search for paid Claude Code skill packs on 闲鱼/淘宝/小报童/知识星球 returned only free GitHub compilations and tutorials.
findings.why_it_matters: Stars and installs are free-tier attention. Any founder bet that counts 'installs' as the pass/fail metric will pass and still make $0; the pass/fail number must be paid seats, paid sales, or a signed fixed-fee engagement.

findings.claim: Freelance-marketplace comparables put a fixed-price 'automation/skills audit' at $499 (Upwork, 5-10 business days, 8-12 page audit + ROI-ranked opportunity map + build priority matrix) and Fiverr lists 24 'Claude skills' gigs; freelance Claude consultants bill $150-300/hour. These are the cheapest priced evidence of small businesses paying for someone else to design their skills.
findings.why_it_matters: A $499-$2,500 'skill audit + rebuild' productized service is the smallest thing a regulated-ops operator can sell in the first 30 days to the business users already asking for Claude-skill workflows; it also generates the fixtures the POC needs.

price_points_observed: Skill files (non-engineer buyers): $3-$10 typical on Agensi, $14.99 KissMySkills, $3.99-$78 Claude Protocol; bundles $15-$25 (Agensi), $63.99-$99 (KissMySkills role bundles, $447.99 everything), $99/501 skills (Claude Protocol)

2) Paid cohort or 2-day live workshop on building skills for operators (bilingual EN/ZH), $500-$1,500/seat, sold to the existing blog/YouTube audience — time-to-first-dollar 2-4 weeks (launch email sequence); comparables sell out at $1,500 with ~50 reviews.

3) $49-$99 skill pack sold from your own site/Gumroad to your own audience — time-to-first-dollar 1-7 days after launch if an audience exists (verified ~$3k in 30-45 days for a 10k-list creator), $0-$300 in 90 days without one; marketplaces (Agensi/KissMySkills) add distribution but median listing <$50/month.

4) Coze (扣子) paid skill listing at 9-99 RMB/month for a Chinese-language ops/finance skill — time-to-first-dollar ~1-3 weeks (5-day review + Alipay/Douyin merchant KYC); evidence of money is loud but secondary, so run it as a cheap portfolio test with a 30-day subscriber count as pass/fail.

5) Tiny one-time-purchase utility ($7-$20) for Claude power users (menu-bar, checker, desktop helper) — time-to-first-dollar days via Product Hunt, but ceiling is hundreds of dollars and Anthropic absorbs the feature; only worth it as a lead magnet for shapes 1-2.

How many of the Maven/DAIR/AI Hero cohort seats are non-engineers, and is there a bilingual (ZH) cohort competitor? None found in Chinese search; 知识星球/小报童 paid Claude Code communities were not surfaced by web search and may need on-platform checks.
Does DingTalk WuKong's 'AI capability market' pay third-party skill developers (revenue share, pricing) — no terms found as of Sep 2026.

Which businesses actually bought the $2.5k-$9.5k Cowork implementation packages (customer counts undisclosed) — worth one call to the vendor or a Product Hunt/LinkedIn scan before pricing the founders' version.
Anthropic Skills API GA (Aug 20, 2026) already does versioning; how soon does Cowork add a native skill manager/history view that kills the 'Cowork skill manager for non-engineers' micro-SaaS idea?

research.topic: Fast, small paid opportunities using regulated wealth/asset-management operations knowledge without an enterprise sale: advisor-facing skill templates, fixed-price AI setups, advisor-tool price anchors, and adjacent Calgary/Alberta small-vertical setups (evidence as of 2026-09-10)

findings.claim: Advisor-specific AI seat prices have compressed to a $50-$120/user/month band, with a self-serve on-ramp now standard: Jump 'Meet' $100/advisor/mo (Onboard +$50, Grow +$50; 'Try for free' button; claims 35,000+ financial professionals), Zocks Essentials $67 / Pro $117 / Ultimate $184 per user/mo with a 14-day credit-card free trial, Wealthbox AI Notetaker add-on $49/user/mo on top of $59-$99 CRM seats, Altruist Hazel ~$50, Finmate ~$76, Zeplyn $60-$120/seat. Kitces 2025 data: Jump+Zocks combined adoption 12.8%, generic Zoom AI/Fathom 7.6%.
findings.why_it_matters: Sets the ceiling for any per-seat micro-SaaS aimed at solo advisors (~$50/mo is the new anchor, and the vendors already self-serve). A 2-person shop cannot win on meeting-prep/notetaking; the money left is in what these vendors do NOT do (proposal, look-through, IPS drift, firm-specific compliance wrapping) and in setup/implementation rather than seats.

findings.claim: A paid 'Claude Skills for financial advisors' product already exists at info-product prices and is a direct comparable: Amplify for Advisors (run by a CFP) sells a skills library subscription at $20/mo, three courses at $99 each ('AI Setup Sprint', 'Voice Guide Launch Pad', 'Consistent Content Blueprint'), a $249 bundle, and 'Amplify for Teams' at $990/yr for up to 10 advisors. Skills are installed into Claude Desktop; the library is content/marketing-focused (voice training, content recycler, quarterly client letters, client email library). No subscriber count disclosed.
findings.why_it_matters: Proves advisors are being sold SKILL.md-style packs at $20/mo + $99 courses today, and that the occupied niche is content/marketing, not operations. An operations pack (proposal, look-through, IPS drift, review prep with compliance wrapping) at the same price points is an open lane; but this is 'attention-scale' money (no revenue disclosed) unless it converts into setup engagements.

findings.claim: Fixed-price 'Claude Cowork setup' as a productized service is live and cheap to start: coworkconsultant.com (independent consultant) advertises 'builds start at $1,500, live in 7 days' (earlier listings: packages from $797), with a Skool community and 1-on-1 sessions; a Canadian MSP (Fusion Computing) markets Claude Cowork deployment to CPA firms (reconciliation, month-end close, first-draft statements) on Team plans at $25/seat with custom consulting; Anthropic's own free wealth-management plugin (client review prep, proposals, rebalancing, client reporting, TLH) installs in Cowork on any paid plan.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'AI setup for your practice' shape is validated at $800-$1,500 for solo operators and delivers in a week; the free Anthropic wealth plugin is the raw material, and the sellable layer is firm-specific configuration + compliance wrapping + data hygiene (Betterment's advisor playbook: 'getting your data into a state skills can rely on is bigger than building the skills').

findings.claim: AI-implementation agencies targeting RIAs price meeting-prep/notes automation at $15K-$30K, prospect-intake at $20K-$50K, 'full advisor co-pilot' $30K-$70K, and full-RIA suites $60K-$150K on a 9-month roadmap; the same agency publishes a Claude-Skills-for-advisors guide (8 workflows incl. IPS drafts, quarterly performance letters, KYC summaries, portfolio review prep) and says 'a three-week rollout is typical for a firm under 20 advisors' with CCO sign-off per skill.
findings.why_it_matters: Gives the mid-market price anchor a 2-person shop can undercut: a single-skill, 1-week, CCO-signed setup at $2.5K-$7.5K sits between the $800 solo setup and the $15K+ agency floor. Note: these are asking prices, not disclosed revenue or client counts.

findings.claim: Canadian AI-consulting rate cards (Apr 2026) for small business: fixed-price 'AI audit/discovery' C$1,500-$5,000, 'Automation Starter' C$2,500-$7,500, 'Custom GPT build' C$3,500-$10,000, AI agent development C$15K-$100K; retainers C$2K/mo (4h) to C$5-10K/mo (fractional AI lead); hourly C$140-$350 for mid/senior boutique. Alberta-specific (Aug/Sep 2026): half-day workshops C$4K-$12K for 8-12 staff, '6-week AI Clarity Sprint' C$15K-$25K, first-year median spend C$15K-$40K for 25-200-employee firms; a Calgary CRM/automation shop quotes CRM projects C$8K-$25K fixed after a free discovery call.
findings.why_it_matters: These are the prices Calgary accounting practices, engineering firms and energy-services SMBs already see from generic agencies; a domain-specific, evidence-backed (fixture + acceptance record) skill setup at C$3K-$10K is priced as a 'Custom GPT build' equivalent and is a known line item, not a new category.

findings.claim: Small-group AI workshops are a proven sub-$1K entry product: a US provider sells half-day workshops at $999 (up to 5 trainees; Claude/ChatGPT + one specialty tool) and full-day at $1,499; Canadian provider chatgpt.ca lists training from C$2,000; Financial Edge sells a 2-day 'Financial Modeling & Valuation Using Claude' course at £995/$1,250 per person; Eventbrite 'Practical Claude Workshop for Finance & Accounting Professionals' sells tickets with a $100 first-10 discount; Advocis CE courses are C$50 members / C$75 non-members.
findings.why_it_matters: A bilingual 'Claude for advisory/asset-management operations' half-day at C$1K-$2.5K per firm (or $99-$250 per seat online) is the fastest cash with the least build; it also functions as top-of-funnel for setup engagements. CE-credit accreditation (Advocis/FP Canada) is a Canadian distribution hook but prices CE content at ~$50-75.

findings.claim: Advisor communities are pay-to-partner channels, not open marketplaces: XYPN (2,100+ members) announces vendor partner benefits (CurrentClient AI call summaries with discounted member pricing, Aug 20 2026; Holistiplan, Orion earlier) through its Partner Program; Schwab launched 'Advisor AI in Action' vendor partnerships via Affinity Services; XYPN's tech page lists partner tools. No evidence of a template/skill marketplace inside XYPN, Kitces or FPA Canada.
findings.why_it_matters: Community distribution requires a formal partner deal (weeks-months) rather than a listing; faster paths are the founders' own content pipeline, direct outreach, and Kitces/AdvisorTech press. Do not plan on 'paid templates on advisor marketplaces' as a 30-day channel.

findings.claim: Advisors do pay recurring money for checklists/templates when packaged as a compliance-safe professional product: fpPathfinder charges $599/year per user (Essentials) with Deluxe/Premier tiers adding white-labeling, interactive checklists and CRM integrations (Redtail, Wealthbox, Salesforce FSC); investment-policy-statement software sells at ~$45-$60/mo and $149/user/mo tiers; manual IPS creation takes ~155 min/client vs 57 min with software (vendor-cited).
findings.why_it_matters: Validates $50/mo-$600/yr template-product pricing in the advisor segment, specifically for the IPS/proposal/checklist artifacts the founders know how to build. A skill pack that emits CCO-reviewable IPS-drift and proposal artifacts can borrow fpPathfinder's white-label + tier pricing.

findings.claim: Generic prompt/skill packs sold on Gumroad/Whop are attention-scale, not income-scale: 2026 Gumroad median creator earns $72/month; prompt packs priced $27-$97 outperform single prompts ~8x in revenue; Notion 'AI finance advisor prompts' template sells at $7.99-$14.99; a 'Generative AI Toolkit for Investment Bankers 2026' sells at $40 on Gumroad. Free finance skill repos (e.g., 81-91 skills across 7 plugins incl. client-review-prep, MIT) sit at ~184 stars; Anthropic's wealth plugin is free.
findings.why_it_matters: Stars and $7-$40 downloads are not money. A finance skill pack should be priced as a professional tool ($20-$50/mo or $99-$249 one-off, per Amplify/fpPathfinder anchors) and used mainly as lead-gen for $1.5K-$10K setups; do not spend build weeks on marketplace listings.

findings.claim: Kitces (2026-09-07) on FINNY's shift to $50/mo + 20 bps (from $6K-$12K/yr flat): 'advisors are willing to pay a percentage of revenue for people or platforms who will deliver new business' but resist paying when 'they're still the ones doing the work'; Kitces (Apr 2026) on Jump's price cut to $100/$75 and modular add-ons: 'what advisors really want is just a well-functioning AI notetaker.' Kitces Research: advisors spend 2-5% of revenue on tech (~$20-50K/yr for a $100M RIA); ~two-thirds have experimented with AI, mostly individual experimentation, not firm-wide.
findings.why_it_matters: Willingness-to-pay rule for this segment: pay for delivered outcomes (a finished proposal, a signed-off IPS review, a filed compliance record), not for tools that add advisor effort. Package the skill as 'done-for-you artifact + setup', not 'a tool you configure'.

findings.claim: Canadian regulatory pull is real but modest for small dealers: CIRO's 2026 Annual Compliance Report says it 'will be inquiring about the use of AI in dealers' operations and reviewing the operational controls' in FinOps exams and expects documented AI use and approved-channel controls; Canadian advisor AI tools market 'CIRO-aligned, PIPEDA, Toronto data residency, SOC 2' (Focal AI) as table stakes; US SEC/FINRA are applying existing supervision/recordkeeping rules with the small-firm compliance date passed 2026-06-03.
findings.why_it_matters: A 'documented AI use + control evidence' deliverable (use-case record, fixtures, acceptance log) is something a small CIRO dealer or portfolio manager can buy now for a few thousand dollars from someone who speaks CCO; it is the differentiator versus generic Calgary automation agencies. Not a mandate that forces purchase, so sell it as a bonus, not the headline.

findings.claim: Calgary/Alberta adjacent verticals have generic agencies but no domain-specific skill sellers: The Automators (Calgary) claims 30+ businesses and 50,000+ manual hours removed across energy/oil & gas, logistics, finance; 42 Labs cites an oil & gas engineering client (RAG/LLM); a Calgary MSP quotes fixed-price after free discovery; Alberta Innovates Micro Voucher ($10K) and Voucher ($100K) intakes are PAUSED since 2026-05-29 (redesign), so no grant-fueled demand in the 30-60 day window.
findings.why_it_matters: Local competition is n8n/Zapier/CRM-sync shops charging C$5K-$25K; a finance-ops-fluent 2-person team can win accounting practices and engineering/energy-services back offices on speed (1-week skill setup) and evidence, but must self-fund the sale (no vouchers now).

findings.claim: Fund-administration / LP-reporting AI is priced far above the 短平快 band: scoped custom automation runs ~$25K-$150K and the 'fluency training that makes it safe to operate' $2K-$15K; incumbents (Allvue, eFront, Investran, Carta) deliver AI features through the administrator rather than direct purchase; 98% of IR professionals use AI weekly (vendor-cited).
findings.why_it_matters: Small fund administrators are a slow, platform-mediated sale; the only fast entry is the $2K-$15K 'fluency/training + one workflow' slice, which is the same workshop+setup shape as advisors. Deprioritize as a first bet.

findings.claim: Schwab's 2026 RIA study (n=533, fielded Oct 2025, published 2026-01-22): 63% of RIAs use AI in some capacity, 82% of those use generative AI, only ~10% have fully integrated AI into strategy; use cases concentrate on notetaking and email drafting; individual experimentation predominates. Betterment's advisor Claude playbook (updated 2026-08-05) lists five skill categories (synthesis/meeting briefs, drafting proposals, portfolio-drift flagging, triage, firm memory) and warns the data-preparation work exceeds the skill-building work.
findings.why_it_matters: The demand gap is 'dabbler → integrated': firms have Claude/ChatGPT seats and free plugins but no one to do the data-shaping, compliance wrapping and firm-specific configuration. That gap is exactly the fixed-price setup job, and custodians (Betterment, Schwab) are now telling advisors to build these skills, which pre-sells the category.

bets.name: Advisor Ops Skill Setup (fixed-price, one workflow, 7 days)
bets.what_exactly: A fixed-price, fixed-scope install of ONE wealth-operations workflow on a small firm's existing Claude Team/Cowork seats, delivered in 5-7 business days: either (a) an investment-proposal pack skill (firm template, product shelf, suitability rationale, disclosure blocks) or (b) a portfolio look-through / holdings roll-up report skill (custodian or PM-system export in, client-ready report out), or (c) client-review-prep. Each deliverable = a private Cowork plugin or Claude Code project skill (1-3 skills), 8-15 fixtures drawn from the client's own historical cases run through the SkillDev POC (fixtures + deterministic rubric + compare/report), a one-page acceptance record (what was tested, what passed, who signed off, model version pinned), one 60-min training session, and a $0 'refresh on next model release' clause that seeds a C$750-1,500/mo retainer. Founder A scopes and reviews the artifact; Founder B builds from the productized starter (Anthropic's free wealth-management plugin + the 32-skill library conventions). This is the day-job demand pattern (business users asking for look-through reports and investment proposals as Claude-skill workflows) resold to OTHER firms of the same type: independent advisors, 2-20 advisor RIAs / portfolio-manager boutiques, family offices and CIRO dealer branches.
bets.buyer_and_price: Buyer: principal, COO or head of operations at a 2-20 person advisory / portfolio-management practice, family office or dealer branch that already pays for Claude Team/Cowork seats (Schwab 2026: 63% of RIAs use AI, ~10% integrated; Betterment/Schwab now telling advisors to build these skills). Price: C$3,500 fixed for one workflow (C$5,500 for two), 50% deposit on kickoff, 50% on acceptance sign-off; optional retainer C$750-1,500/mo for maintenance on model updates and one new skill per quarter. Sits between the $1,500 solo Cowork setups and the $15k+ agency floor.
bets.six_month_revenue_realistic: C$20k-45k: 4-8 paid setups at C$3.5-5.5k plus 2-3 retainers at ~C$1k/mo starting month 3; upside C$60k if two setups per month from month 3. Founder B capacity caps this at ~2 setups/month (each ~15-20 evening hours).
bets.demand_evidence: Fixed-fee Cowork/skills installs already sell at $2,500-9,500 with 'live in ~2 weeks' (Wellforce) and $2,000-5,000 + $500-1,500/mo retainers with explicit ICP of financial advisory and consultancies 2-50 people (8th Street) [productized-services:F1][productized-services:F2]; an advisor-specific implementer publishes the exact skill menu buyers respond to (IPS, quarterly letters, KYC, proposal, portfolio review prep) at $15k-30k+ with 3-week rollouts and CCO sign-off per skill, leaving the C$2.5-7.5k single-skill slot open [domain-quick-wins:F4][productized-services:F10]; coworkconsultant.com sells builds 'from $1,500, live in 7 days' [domain-quick-wins:F3]; Kitces: advisors pay for delivered outcomes, not tools that add effort, so 'done-for-you artifact + setup' is the right packaging [domain-quick-wins:F10]; 63% of RIAs use AI but ~10% integrated, and the vendor gives the raw wealth plugin away, leaving configuration, data shaping and firm-specific wrapping as the paid gap [domain-quick-wins:F14][productized-services:F4][vertical:F3]; Canadian platforms (Conquest, d1g1t, Croesus, OneVest) all shipped MCP servers and leave the firm-side workflow layer to others [vertical:F2][vertical:F15]; round-1 concluded services are the only path with meaningful year-1 cash for a part-time team [business-model:F13]; small-firm regulated buyers scope prompts/agent workflows into first-line roles and will accept a pre-deployment test record with human sign-off [verify:C9][verify:C4].
bets.why_these_founders: Founder A has built exactly these artifacts (look-through reports, investment proposals) inside a regulated asset manager and has business users asking for them as skill workflows — nobody selling Cowork installs today has that operations depth (Blend2Balance is FP&A, Layer3 is generic advisor marketing/ops). Founder B's SkillDev POC turns each engagement's fixtures and compare/report into the acceptance record in hours, which is the differentiator vs Calgary n8n/Zapier shops. Calgary base gives in-person access to local advisory practices and dealer branches; the bilingual blog/YouTube pipeline is the inbound funnel. Two part-time people can deliver one setup in ~20 combined hours.
bets.thirty_day_test_pass_fail: PASS: 1 signed engagement with a collected deposit >= C$1,750 by day 30, from >= 6 booked discovery calls (warm network + one published 'proposal skill in 7 days' blog/video with a booking link). FAIL: 0 deposits collected by day 30, or fewer than 3 discovery calls despite 20 direct outreach messages.
bets.what_it_teaches_if_it_fails: Whether small wealth firms will pay a third party for firm-specific configuration when the vendor's plugin is free (DIY vs done-for-you), whether the founders' warm network actually contains 5+ reachable small-firm decision makers, and whether the 'acceptance record' is valued or ignored by small-firm buyers. A fail with calls-but-no-deposits says the price or the scope is wrong (retest at C$1,500 audit-style); a fail with no calls says the channel is wrong and the cohort/content bets must run first.
bets.twelve_month_durability: Durable as a services line: repeat triggers are model releases (re-test + refresh), new workflows and new advisors joining; the retainer layer at 5-8 clients is C$5-10k/mo. Ceiling for two part-time people is ~C$100-150k/yr, not a company. Risks: Anthropic's free wealth plugin and Cowork 'build from template' keep lowering DIY cost; agencies (Layer3, Phos) may add a sub-$10k tier; mitigations are the acceptance-record/fixture discipline and the operator credibility, which generic shops lack. Every engagement produces reusable fixtures for the ops template pack (Bet 4).

bets.name: Skills Audit + Cowork Install for professional-services firms (Calgary + audience)
bets.what_exactly: A two-rung productized service for 5-50 person professional-services firms (CPA practices, law firms, consultancies, engineering/energy-services back offices) that already have Claude Team/Cowork or Claude Code seats. Rung 1: a $749 fixed 'Skills Audit' delivered in 5 business days — inventory every skill/plugin in the firm's Cowork or Claude Code, run 3-5 fixtures per skill through the SkillDev POC to record which skills fire and what they produce, dedupe the 'junk drawer', rewrite trigger descriptions, and hand back a before/after report plus a ranked list of 8-15 workflows that recur 4+ times/month. Rung 2: a C$4,500 fixed 'Cowork install' (2-3 weeks) — 8-15 firm-specific skills packaged as a private Cowork plugin, 2-3 connectors (M365/Google, QuickBooks or practice-management export), two training sessions, a one-page AI-use policy, and an acceptance record; optional C$750/mo retainer. Founder B delivers; Founder A runs discovery and the policy/training layer.
bets.buyer_and_price: Buyer: managing partner, practice manager or ops lead at a 5-50 person Calgary/Alberta professional-services firm, or a reader of the blog/YouTube pipeline who runs one. Price: Audit $749 (US$) fixed, paid up front; Install C$4,500 fixed (50/50), priced as the local 'Custom GPT build / Automation Starter' line item (C$2.5-10k); retainer C$750-1,500/mo.
bets.six_month_revenue_realistic: C$15k-30k: 8-12 audits at ~$750 (C$8-12k) converting roughly 1 in 3 into 3-4 installs at C$4.5k (C$13-18k), plus 1-2 retainers by month 5. The audit alone never exceeds ~C$2k/mo; the install conversion is the money.
bets.demand_evidence: Documented, unresolved pain: 73% of 214 audited community skills scored <60/100 and 'most failed silently'; business users complain skills 'are all loading at once'; practitioners recommend 8-15 skills max before the list becomes a junk drawer [productized-services:F5]; a $499 fixed Claude 'automation audit' (5-10 business days) is already sold on Upwork and clients post 'Set up Claude Code' / 'Claude Code Training' as sub-one-month gigs [productized-services:F8][micro-saas-and-tooling:F13]; Anthropic's free Claude for Small Business plugin leaves the paid gaps as operational training, connector setup and 'how to recover when a workflow misfires' [productized-services:F4]; fixed-fee Cowork installs at $2,000-9,500 with the same deliverable list (skills library + training + AI policy) exist with explicit CPA/law/advisory ICPs [productized-services:F1][productized-services:F2][micro-saas-and-tooling:F5]; Canadian rate cards put AI audit at C$1.5-5k and Automation Starter at C$2.5-7.5k, and Calgary competition is generic n8n/Zapier shops with no evidence discipline; Alberta vouchers are paused so buyers self-fund [domain-quick-wins:F5][domain-quick-wins:F12]; a Canadian MSP already markets Cowork to CPA firms on Team seats [domain-quick-wins:F3]; 'did it fire' trigger tooling exists only free, so the money shape is the service, not a checker [micro-saas-and-tooling:F7]; SMB per-workflow builds at $2.5-12k and retainers $500-2,000/mo are market norms [productized-services:F6].
bets.why_these_founders: The SkillDev POC (fixtures, deterministic rubrics, compare/report, editorial review workspace) IS the audit tool — the $749 report is generated from evidence the POC already produces, so the audit costs Founder B ~4-6 hours. Founder A's own 32-skill audit lesson ('23 gates, 5 checked; failures should become scripts') is the pitch. Founder B's pushback-on-AI judgment is what a managing partner is buying in a 'which of these skills actually work' report. Calgary base allows in-person closes; the content pipeline supplies inbound audits from the EN/ZH audience.
bets.thirty_day_test_pass_fail: PASS: 3 paid audits (>= $2,000 collected) by day 30 AND at least 1 install proposal requested. FAIL: fewer than 2 paid audits after 25 direct outreach messages to firms known to have Claude seats plus one published audit-report sample.
bets.what_it_teaches_if_it_fails: Whether SMB professional-services firms on Cowork feel 'my skills don't fire / produce junk' as a budgeted pain or a shrug (revealed WTP for evidence at the smallest ticket); whether the audit converts to installs (if audits sell but installs don't, the evidence report is a curiosity not a purchase driver); and whether a cold-ish Calgary channel can produce leads in 30 days without grants.
bets.twelve_month_durability: The audit rung erodes within 2-4 quarters as /skill-doctor and `claude plugin eval` GA give firms free self-checks; the install + retainer rung is durable because configuration, connectors, training and policy stay human work and every model release re-triggers a refresh. Expect the audit to become a free lead magnet by month 6-9 and the install to be the product. Ceiling ~C$60-100k/yr part-time; retainers at 6-8 clients give ~C$5-8k/mo.

Each participant leaves with two working skills on their own seats plus the founders' fixture/acceptance-record templates. Recordings + templates sold afterwards as a self-paced product, and a ZH-subtitled recorded track for the Chinese-speaking audience at 中文 price points. Sold through the existing blog/YouTube/X pipeline and LinkedIn, with Luma/Stripe checkout; no platform build.
bets.buyer_and_price: Buyer: individual professionals paying personally or on small L&D budgets — ops managers, product/BA staff, paraplanners, compliance-ops and fund-admin analysts at small and mid-size wealth/asset-management firms (EN, North America); Chinese-speaking finance-ops professionals for the recorded track. Price: US$549 early / US$749 list per seat (finance-persona comps $499-799); team of 3 for $1,299; self-paced recording $149; ZH recorded track ¥299-599 (中文 course ceiling is ~1/5-1/8 of EN).
bets.six_month_revenue_realistic: US$14k-24k: two live cohorts at 12-18 paid seats x ~$549 average ($13-20k) plus $1.5-4k of recordings and a few hundred dollars from the ZH track. Third cohort possible in month 6. This is the highest-margin bet per founder hour (~40 h prep, ~10 h delivery per cohort).
bets.demand_evidence: Finance-professional Claude cohorts fill at $499-799: Blend2Balance 'Claude in Action' (4 x 60 min) marked its Sept 2 cohort FULL and claims 1,000+ finance professionals trained, with buyers citing 'build a skill for my own reconciliation/reporting task' as the deliverable [info-products:F3]; Maven 'Claude for Non-Technical Operators' $799 with 63 reviews at 4.9 and 'Claude Code in Practice' $1,500 SOLD OUT with 54 reviews prove operators pay high-ticket for live, persona-specific instruction [info-products:F2][micro-saas-and-tooling:F4]; vendor education is free (Anthropic Academy, Tessl Academy), so only domain/persona-specific content retains price [info-products:F7][info-products:F4]; a $1,250/person 2-day 'Financial Modeling using Claude' course exists, confirming finance-vertical price tolerance [domain-quick-wins:F6]; non-technical operators are an explicitly paying segment for skills/Cowork instruction [info-products:F12]; pre-existing audience is the verified precondition for money in 30-45 days ($3k pack sales to a 10k list; $0-300 without one) [micro-saas-and-tooling:F3]; the Chinese market pays for 'AI海外赚钱' framing (16k subs at ¥10) and Chinese media eagerly translate Anthropic finance skills, but investment-advice framing is now policed on 知识星球/头条, so the operations framing is the safe lane [info-products:F10][info-products:F11]; cohort alumni are the warm pipeline for Bet 1 (audit-to-retainer conversion) [productized-services:F9].
bets.why_these_founders: Founder A can teach the actual artifacts (proposal, look-through, compliance dashboard) from the operator's chair, in EN and 中文, which no current seller does (Blend2Balance = accounting/FP&A; Maven = generic operators). FAIL: fewer than 6 paid seats by day 30 (refund the deposits, ship the material as the Bet 4 template pack, and treat the audience as not yet monetizable at $500+).
bets.what_it_teaches_if_it_fails: The single most important unknown: whether the founders' audience converts to money, and at what ticket. Seats sold vs landing-page visits gives a conversion rate that prices every later info product; a fail at $549 with strong signups at $149 recordings says the audience is 中文/consumer-weighted rather than EN professional; zero interest says the wealth-ops persona is not in the audience and Bets 1-2 must be sold by outreach, not content.
bets.twelve_month_durability: Repeatable 3-4 times per year with content refresh at each model/Cowork release (which is also the re-buy trigger for alumni). Ceiling ~US$40-70k/yr at 20 seats per cohort, more if a $29-49/mo alumni community (Skool-style) is added after cohort 2. Free vendor education and B站 tutorials cap generic content, but the finance-ops persona and the founders' live judgment are not reproducible. Risk: a bigger finance-training brand adds an asset-management track; mitigation is speed and the acceptance-record angle.

gens.angle: Info products, cohorts, communities and paid skill packs sold through the existing bilingual (EN/ZH) blog + YouTube pipeline and personal audience. Ranking rule from the evidence: money in this segment goes to (a) live instruction for a named non-developer persona at $500-$1,500/seat, (b) the service layer around a skill pack ($499 audit -> $2.5-9.5k install), and (c) mass-priced Chinese columns framed as '海外AI操盘手/用AI赚钱', not tool tutorials. Free packs, $30 courses, newsletters and marketplaces are funnels, not bets. The four bets below are sized so the founders run 2-3 in parallel (cohort + pack/support is the recommended pair; the Chinese column rides the same content hours; the harness template is the lowest-conviction test and should be run last or as a stretch).

bets.name: Operator Skills Cohort (EN): 'Run your work on Claude Code / Codex skills' for finance-ops and non-technical operators
bets.what_exactly: A 2-week live cohort, 4 x 90-min sessions + Discord/office hours, capped at 20 seats, taught by Founder A (operator voice) with Founder B running the technical lab. Curriculum: (1) turn a recurring task into a SKILL.md that fires reliably (description/trigger discipline), (2) build the skill from 3-5 real past deliverables as fixtures and check 'did it fire / what did it produce' with the POC's before/after review pack, (3) chain skills into a workflow (proposal pack, look-through QA, monthly report, meeting recap) on Claude Code, Codex and Cowork, (4) keep it alive across model releases (fixture re-run, prune/keep). Every student leaves with 2 working skills and a fixture set. Pre-sold via a landing page + 3 blog posts + 2 YouTube videos + an X thread; recordings kept for enrolled students only (sell live access, not recordings). Positioning explicitly avoids what Anthropic/Tessl give away free ('how skills work') and sells the operator's judgment plus the finance-ops examples.
bets.buyer_and_price: Buyer: non-technical operators and finance/ops professionals (analysts, controllers, advisors' ops staff, consultants, solo founders) already on a paid Claude/ChatGPT plan, reached via the founders' EN audience and LinkedIn. Price: C$699 list / C$549 early-bird (USD ~$500-$520), between Blend2Balance's $499 sale and Maven's $799 non-technical certification; a 'team of 3' ticket at C$1,800.
bets.six_month_revenue_realistic: C$20k-45k gross: cohort 1 (Oct) 12-20 seats, cohort 2 (Nov/Dec) 15-25 seats, cohort 3 (Feb) 15-25 seats at ~C$600 average; midpoint ~C$30k. Add C$3-8k if 2-3 alumni convert to a paid firm install (bet 3).
bets.demand_evidence: Premium 2-week Claude Code cohorts sell at $499-$799 and the closest comp, Maven's 'Claude for Non-Technical Operators' at $799, has 63 reviews at 4.9/5 (~$50k+ gross across runs) [key:info-products F2]; Maven 'Claude Code in Practice' at $1,500 is sold out with 54 five-star reviews and DAIR's non-technical cohort sells at $899 [key:micro-saas F4]. Finance-professional Claude cohorts fill: Blend2Balance's Sept 2 cohort at $499/$799 marked FULL, '1,000+ finance professionals trained', with 'build a skill for my own reconciliation' as the cited deliverable [key:info-products F3]. Non-developers are the explicitly targeted paying persona ($799 Maven, $9-97/mo Skool, beginner workshops) while individual developers do not pay [key:info-products F12][verify:C8]. Vendor education is free (Anthropic Academy 17 courses, Tessl Academy), so the price holds only for persona-specific, live, judgment-heavy formats [key:info-products F7][key:info-products F4]. The reference EN ladder (free skills repo -> newsletter -> $795 cohort) is Matt Pocock's, and pirated resale of his cohort signals real demand [key:info-products F6]. Founders' own audit: attention accrues to packs and content, monetization to instruction/access [gapfill-4:F12][open-source:F10].
bets.why_these_founders: Founder A already runs the bilingual blog+YouTube pipeline (the funnel exists; no ad spend), has 32 production skills to teach from, and the regulated wealth-ops examples (look-through, proposals, compliance dashboards) that no current cohort seller has (Blend2Balance is accounting/FP&A). Business users at the day job already ask for exactly this, which is the persona test. Founder B's POC editorial-review workspace and fixture protocol become the lab exercise ('failed deliverable becomes a fixture in <10 min' is a session). Time fits: ~10 h/week for Founder A during the 2 live weeks, one evening/week for Founder B.
bets.thirty_day_test_pass_fail: PASS: >=10 paid seats at >=C$549 (>=C$5,490 collected, refunds excluded) by day 30 from a launch sequence of 3 posts + 2 videos + 1 email. FAIL: <6 paid seats, or >50% of buyers are developers rather than operators (wrong persona). Kill the cohort format if fail; keep the content.
bets.what_it_teaches_if_it_fails: Whether the founders' audience is buyers or readers (list size vs. paid conversion), whether the operator persona is reachable without LinkedIn/Maven distribution, and whether 'finance-ops on skills' is a price-holding niche or already commoditized by free vendor courses. Also produces the seat-price and persona data needed before any community (Skool) or template bet.
bets.twelve_month_durability: Medium-low. Cohorts are repeatable (4-6 runs/year) and priced on live access, which pirated recordings cannot replace, but each run costs ~40 founder hours and the 'how to' layer erodes as Anthropic/Tessl expand free curricula. Durable only if it feeds a retention layer (alumni community at $29-49/mo or firm installs). Expect price pressure to C$400-500 by mid-2027 unless the finance-ops specialization is kept sharp.

judges.judge_lens: Indie hacker who has bootstrapped several products and productized services to $5-30k MRR within months. I score on what actually collects a first dollar in 30 days from two part-time people with no sales team: can you sell it on one call to a warm contact, can you deliver it with what already exists (the POC, the 32 skills, the content pipeline, Founder A's operator credibility), and does the 30-day number teach you where the money is. Durability included in the sum but only used as a tie-breaker. Two priors from the evidence drive the scores: (a) packs/templates/directories earn stars, not cash — the verified best case is ~$3k in 30-45 days for a 10k-list creator, $0-300 without a list — so every self-serve pack is a lead magnet at best; (b) the fastest cash in this ecosystem is a fixed-fee thing sold to a warm contact (audits $499-1,500 in days, installs $2.5-9.5k in 2-4 weeks) and a persona-specific live cohort pre-sold to an existing audience (finance cohorts fill at $499-799). The biggest unknown across all 16 bets is whether the founders' audience converts to money at all; the cheapest way to learn that is a presale, not a product.

Weeks 2-4: deliver 1-3 audits at 4-6 h each. BET C — Advisor Ops Skill Setup (#1), Founder A's remaining 3-4 h/week plus Founder B post-deposit.
