Incumbents do not buy schemas from unknown two-person teams; they adopt open ones or write their own, and the exact slot this bet targets is being filled for free right now: in-toto already has a test-result predicate and an open agent-decision predicate with evaluation_results fields (opened 2026-05-19 by a small vendor, still unmerged after ~4 months, which shows even a zero-dollar standards contribution takes quarters, not 30 days); OTel GenAI conventions already define invoke_agent/execute_tool spans and were split into a dedicated repo in June 2026; AWS ships strands-agents/evals under Apache-2.0 that already reads Claude Code/Codex/Gemini transcripts; agentskills maintainers merged eval-contract docs and evals.json validation for free; and on 2026-09-05 another indie published an MIT 'versioned evidence schema for agent skills' with zero adoption. The POC is private, unlicensed, unpublished, three weeks old, with zero external users and zero adoption signal, so the only forms in which a JFrog/Google/Tessl PM could say yes are (a) 'contribute it upstream for $0' or (b) an acqui-hire, which requires full-time founders. Round-1 base rates confirm: Anthropic's Humanloop deal acquired no IP and killed the product; Smithery exited quietly after 18 months on undisclosed terms; Tessl retains only scores (not traces), is coding-only, and is pivoting to Agent/Code Review/Academy; Google's registry does structural validation only; JFrog's 'evidence' is security provenance inside AppTrust, and the eval-status slot is 'feature-sized' and something JFrog would build itself. Even a willing incumbent's BD, security review, legal and IP-assignment cycle alone exceeds 60 days. Net: the probability of a paying customer for this bet inside 60 days is near zero, and the founders would spend engineer hours making the POC presentable to buyers who have a free path.
evidence: Round-2 own sizing of the evidence-schema play: '12-mo revenue: $0-$45k (0-3 design partners at $15k) with 6-12 month regulated sales cycles; most likely $0 in the first 12 months from the standard itself... value is optionality... partnership or acqui-hire' (w2-digest.md line 834) and 'sell nothing for 12 months', '$0 by design' (w2-digest.md lines 959-967). All three judges scored schema stewardship 'cheap, reputational, not revenue' (w2-digest.md line 251).

Acquirer base rate: Anthropic acqui-hired Humanloop Aug 2025 and shut the product Sep 8 2025 (no IP acquired per bear angle line 681); Smithery acquired by Arcade 2026-08-05 'no terms disclosed' after ~18 months and a pivot (w1 open-source F11); sub-scale eval tools exit as acqui-hire or maintenance mode, and 'the most likely acquirer/absorber is the harness vendor itself' (w1 startups F1, F2).

Incumbents' actual posture in the slot: JFrog's AI Catalog 'scans, verifies, signs' but 'nothing in JFrog's registry records whether a skill works or regressed' (w1-digest line 1169-1170); C6 verification: 'Prompt to Release Traceability' is an AppTrust feature, 'in-toto' and 'two-stage' were round-1 glosses not JFrog wording (w2-digest lines 64-67, 469). Google Skill Registry: immutable revisions, structural validation only, billed from 2026-09-01. Tessl: retains scores/activation/cost, NOT transcripts or tool-call traces; coding-only taxonomy; pivoting to Agent/Code Review/Academy (w1-brief §C). 'Nobody links eval results to a skill version in a registry — that slice is open but feature-sized' (w1-brief §B).

Already free: in-toto/attestation has a maintained test-result predicate and an open RFC #554 'agent-decision/v0.1' predicate with evaluation_results and trace_parent fields, opened 2026-05-19 by Auxidus Technologies, still open with no maintainer response as of 2026-09-10 (https://github.com/in-toto/attestation/issues/554; https://github.com/in-toto/attestation/blob/main/spec/predicates/test-result.md). OTel GenAI semantic conventions define invoke_agent/chat/execute_tool span nesting and were moved to a dedicated GenAI repo at v1.42.0 (2026-06-12), pre-stable (https://greptime.com/blogs/2026-05-09-opentelemetry-genai-semantic-conventions; https://uptrace.dev/blog/opentelemetry-ai-systems). AWS strands-agents/evals (Apache-2.0) already reads Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLI/OpenHands transcripts client-side (w1-brief §B, gapfill-6:F1-F4).

Competing free schema published 5 days before today: 'A Versioned Evidence Schema for Agent Skills: Provenance, Permissions, Task Fit, and Test Status' (dev.to, 2026-09-05, open-source, no vendor adoption, one real skill) — shows the idea is not scarce and the market price of an unadopted schema is $0 (https://dev.to/leoautomotiveai/a-versioned-evidence-schema-for-agent-skills-provenance-permissions-task-fit-and-test-status-3o04).

Standards cadence contradicts the 30-60 day clock: agentskills maintainers merge docs (#364, #363) but an open naming inconsistency (#459, PR #506) sits unclosed; round-1 verdict 'the way to occupy the seat is to propose it upstream, not to keep it private' (gapfill-3:F7). AGENTS.md converged across vendors and 'produced no standalone business' (w1 historical F12).

Asset state: the POC is 'private, unlicensed, unpublished', ~5.9k LOC, built Aug 23-Sep 7 2026, Ollama adapter only, no external user has yet understood it without founder context (context-pack §2a). The observability substrate it exports from is undocumented and moving (C2: Claude Code masks skill names on OTel, hooks are a fragile workaround; Codex implicit skill choice not observable, w1-brief §H).

Absorption risk on the incumbent side: OTel cost-metric redaction is 'intentional' and Anthropic is 'considering aligning' (gapfill-3:F1-F5); a vendor can close the gap 'with one flag' (w2-digest line 992). A buyer would rather wait for that than license from a two-person part-time team.

Founder capacity: engineer 10-15 h/week, operator 5-7 h/week (constraints-update §3); JFrog partner onboarding involves partner managers, training and portal processes with no published turnaround (https://jfrog.com/technology-partner/), i.e. a BD cycle, not a 30-day sale.
refutations.restated_bet: Strongest surviving form: 'Six Emails as paid-integration discovery, not licensing.' Publish the schema + cross-harness exporter as an MIT repo (with an in-toto predicate draft and three public skills carrying evidence bundles) so there is something an incumbent PM can point at, then email six named owners (JFrog AI Catalog PM, Google Skill Registry PM, Tessl, AWS strands-agents/evals maintainers, Snyk Evo, Caliper/Alibaba skill-up maintainers) with one concrete, small ask each: a fixed-fee 4-week adapter/integration engagement ($5-15k) or a listed technology-partner slot, not a license. Treat it as a ≤25-hour reputational side-bet that rides alongside a real revenue bet (services/workflow package), never as one of the 2-3 portfolio slots. Expected direct revenue in 60 days ≈ $0; the payoff is a citable reference position and inbound for the services bet.
refutations.thirty_day_test_revised: Days 1-7 (engineer ≤15 h): publish the evidence schema + exporter (Claude Code hooks/stream-json, Gemini activate_skill, Codex explicit $skill) as an MIT repo with 3 public skills carrying evidence bundles, one CI example, and a draft in-toto predicate; open the agentskills docs PR. Day 7 (operator ≤4 h): send six emails to named PMs/maintainers with a single ask: fixed-fee 4-week adapter engagement ($5-15k) or listed partnership; include the repo link and a 90-second demo. Days 8-30 (≤6 h total, no further build): reply only, do not build on spec. Day-30 PASS = at least one signed scoped paid engagement ≥$5k OR (one maintainer merging/citing the schema AND ≥2 substantive replies from named PMs asking for a call). FAIL = zero PM replies, or only 'contribute it upstream' replies, or any reply that asks for SOC 2/security review before a conversation — then freeze the repo at zero hours/week and redirect all engineer time to the revenue bet. Hard cap: 25 combined hours; if exceeded before Day 30, it has already failed.

refutations.candidate: #3 Claude for Wealth & Asset-Management Operations live cohort (EN + ZH recorded)
refutations.strongest_attack: A public cohort needs an audience the founders do not have, and the ZH track sells into a market where the product is banned. Founder A's own content-strategy doc (src/content/strategy/x.md) is written from "0 followers"; no subscriber/follower/view counts appear anywhere in the brain, and its Phase 3 ("first $1K from products", first $49-99 playbook) is explicitly gated on 10k followers / 2,000 email subscribers at months 6-12 — none of the phase checkboxes are ticked. Maven's own launch guidance says first-cohort landing pages convert at ~0.5% (rising to 1-2% with testimonials) and need 100-300 targeted views/week; filling even 10 seats of a niche "wealth-ops" cohort in 30 days therefore needs ~1,000-2,000 qualified landing visits from finance-ops people, which a 3-4 h/week content pipeline with no owned list cannot generate cold. Meanwhile the general layer is free (Claude Academy, 31 free courses incl. Agent Skills/Cowork, launched 2026-08-21; Anthropic's free 'Claude for Investing Teams' webinar and free Wealth Management plugin), and the paid finance-training layer is already served by credentialed brands with distribution (Financial Edge: $1,250 2-day live Claude course taught by a CFA ex-Merrill analyst; Graduate School USA: $899, 3-day, 1.8 CEUs, explicitly targeting 'wealth management professionals, compliance officers, financial operations staff'). The ZH recording doubles production effort for near-zero incremental buyers: claude.ai and the API are unavailable in mainland China (and reportedly HK), and Anthropic tightened restrictions on Chinese-controlled entities in July 2026 with ID verification — a Chinese-speaking wealth-ops professional who can legally use Claude at work is an overseas-Chinese sliver. Finally the bet uses the wrong asset: a live cohort burns all of Founder A's 5-7 h/week (prep + delivery + marketing for 6-8 weeks) while Founder B's engineering speed — the team's strongest asset — sits idle.
evidence: Founders' own strategy doc src/content/strategy/x.md: 'Reply Strategy (The #1 Growth Hack at 0 Followers)'; Phase 1 target 1,000 followers/100 subscribers, Phase 3 (months 6-12) '10,000+ followers, 2,000+ email subscribers, first $1K from products' — no phase items checked; grep of brain/journal, reviews, goals finds no subscriber/follower/view numbers at all.

Maven Help Center (help.maven.com 'Guide to successfully market your course'): initial conversion 'as low as 0.5%' until landing page refined and testimonials collected; target 1-2%; courses with >100 landing views/week are 50% more likely to fill a first cohort; recommends 300 views/week. => 10 seats at 1% needs ~1,000 qualified visits inside the 30-day window.

Free substitutes: Claude Academy launched 2026-08-21 with 31 free courses across Claude.ai, Cowork, Claude Code, Agent Skills, MCP (spectrumailab.com, devtoolhub.com, aiagentslibrary.com); Anthropic runs a free 'Claude for Investing Teams' webinar (anthropic.com/webinars) and gives away the Wealth Management plugin (claude.com/plugins/wealth-management). W1 brief E: Anthropic pushes finance skill libraries free (Citadel, BNY, Carlyle, Mizuho, FactSet named).

Paid incumbents with credentials and distribution: Financial Edge 'Financial Modeling & Valuation Using Claude' live online, £995/$1,250 for 2 days, CFA/PhD ex-Merrill instructor (fe.training); Graduate School USA 'AI for Financial Services' $899, 3 days, live or self-paced, 1.8 CEUs, audience 'financial advisors, analysts, portfolio managers, compliance officers, wealth management professionals, and financial operations staff' (graduateschool.edu).

ZH market: mainland China not in Claude's supported locations; claude.ai blocked, api.anthropic.com unreachable without VPN (jilo.ai, teamorouter.com, May 2026); Anthropic closed offshore/subsidiary loopholes for Chinese-controlled entities July 2026 and rolled out government-ID verification for flagged accounts from April 2026 (Investing.com/FT, BanklessTimes 2026-07-03); Hong Kong also reported blocked (doodhk.com).

synth.one_paragraph: Run a three-rung services ladder sold on one call to one warm list, and stop building product. All three judges converge on the same top cluster in different order (audit 25/26/26, single-workflow install 26/25/26, cohort 27/26/25), and the refuter did not touch the first two; it weakened the cohort (the founders' own strategy doc is written from "0 followers", Claude Academy gives the generic layer away free, credentialed incumbents sell finance Claude courses at $899-1,250) and killed the two passive options (do-nothing baseline, four-emails schema licence) and the paid pack. So month 1 is: (1) a $750/$1,500 Did-It-Fire Skill Audit behind a free 20-minute triage, (2) a C$3,500 one-workflow Advisor Ops install with zero build until a 50% deposit lands, (3) a C$2,500-4,000 firm-paid wealth-ops workshop offered on the same call instead of a public presale. Every pass/fail counts cash collected or a signed SOW, never installs, stars or calls. The market evidence caps this at a C$50-150k/yr services line for two part-timers, not a company; its job is to find out in 30 days whether the warm network exists, whether anyone pays for evidence (triage taken but $750 refused = evidence priced at $0), and whether "done-for-you artifact + acceptance record" beats the vendor's free wealth plugin. The SkillDev POC becomes the report generator behind rung 1 and the acceptance-record generator behind rung 2, frozen at 20% of Founder B's hours; if no rung has collected C$5k by day 60, stop and keep the POC as internal tooling.

synth.what_the_poc_becomes: A delivery tool, not the product. Under this plan the POC has exactly two jobs: (1) the report generator behind the audit (inspect/manifest normalizer + fixture runner + deterministic checks + compare/report + editorial review workspace rendered as a static HTML keep/fix/prune pack a COO can read), and (2) the acceptance-record generator behind the install and workshop (fixtures from the client's own past deliverables, run.json, before/after artifact diff, sign-off block with model version pinned). Freeze the surface this week: keep the evidence bundle, fixture protocol, deterministic rubrics, Git-pinned regression report and reviewer diff; delete the graph viewer, Ollama adapter, self-iterate pillar and any cloud/auth/billing/telemetry ambition; adopt `claude plugin eval` cases/graders and skill-creator evals.json as the native runner and interchange rather than maintaining a parallel loop [verify:C1][platform-absorption:F12]. Cap Founder B at 20% of his hours on the POC; the other 80% delivers audits and installs. The only durable thing it accumulates is the per-firm fixture library minted from real deliverables, which is the small data gravity that makes the retainer (bet 5) sellable and that no Calgary MSP or generic agency has. If by day 60 no rung has collected C$5k, the POC reverts to internal tooling for the founders' own 32 skills and the blog harness, and the four-emails schema play stays a weekend PR at most. Explicitly abandoned: any Skill IDE, hosted eval service, SaaS-factory or 'Sentry for skills' framing; the round-2 verdict that the POC is not the differentiated asset stands (the differentiated assets are Founder A's operations depth, the warm network if it exists, and Founder B's delivery speed).
